about: Author-editable reading routes for the Bridge site. The site reads this file at load time; edit it and reload the page. Routes appear in the order listed; the first route is the one expanded on the home page.

standing_values.INTERFACE_DRAFT: Written by the interface, awaiting author review. Shown to readers as 'Draft route'.
standing_values.AUTHOR_CURATED: Chosen and ordered by the author. Shown to readers as 'From the author'.

routes.title: Start with the failure
routes.intro: Seven papers, starting from a failure most readers recognize and ending with the software you use. Each stop builds on the one before it.

stops.why: Starts with a failure you have probably seen: something presented as authorized when no valid warrant path exists. The rest of the route is about preventing it.
Gives that failure a grammar: when partial evidence, successful runs, or repeated use may, and may not, escalate into claims of correctness.
Applies the grammar to AI reasoning. Outputs count as authorized state only through explicit, auditable admission events.
Moves from authority to meaning. Meaning is a typed, scoped binding, and whether a binding exists is a separate question from whether it is true or admissible.
Turns bindings into a substrate: a meaning base that stores and revises semantic entries without collapsing source, identity, evidence, and standing.
The execution side. A kernel that asks which authority can bind a decision, and records admission, refusal, and effect as reviewable history.
Ends with what this means for the software you run: control requires being able to determine its meaning, constrain its effects, and replace its suppliers.
